meta.name: HEOSAT
meta.about: Apereo's Higher Education Open Source Assessment Toolkit as a standing self-assessment, generated from heosat-evidence-map.json. The tool's rubric (2026.07 enhanced guidance edition) scores 47 questions in 9 sections; each question links to the parts of HAX that answer it. 33 evidenced (green), 12 partial (amber, in progress) and 2 gaps (ghosted, dashed). A self-assessment for maintainer review, not a HEOSAT score.

hs_ll.desc: Legal & Licensing: 5 questions. 4 evidenced, 1 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_gv.desc: Governance & Decision-Making: 7 questions. 4 evidenced, 1 partial, 2 gaps.

hs_ce.desc: Community Engagement: 5 questions. 4 evidenced, 1 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_do.desc: Documentation & Onboarding: 5 questions. 2 evidenced, 3 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_po.desc: Project Operations & Roadmap: 5 questions. 3 evidenced, 2 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_sr.desc: Security & Risk Management: 5 questions. 5 evidenced, 0 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_as.desc: Accessibility, Standards & Interoperability: 5 questions. 5 evidenced, 0 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_ai.desc: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit: 5 questions. 2 evidenced, 3 partial, 0 gaps.

hs_fs.desc: Financial & Organizational Sustainability: 5 questions. 4 evidenced, 1 partial, 0 gaps.

hq_ll1.desc: The project is distributed with a clearly identified Open Source Initiative (OSI) Approved Open Source License ®.

hq_ll2.desc: Every repository and distributed artifact includes license and copyright notices. License files ship in every core repo. Per-file headers are not checked yet; a weekly license compliance job that would check them is planned.

hq_ll3.desc: The project documents third-party dependencies and their licenses. A blocking PR-time dependency license check is planned, not yet in CI.

hq_ll4.desc: The project has a documented contributor licensing or contribution agreement policy.

hq_ll5.desc: The project explains trademark, name, logo, and brand usage expectations.

hq_gv1.desc: The project has a public governance model describing roles, authority, and decision-making processes.

hq_gv2.desc: The project records significant technical and community decisions in public venues.

hq_gv3.desc: The project has a defined process for adding, reviewing, and removing maintainers or committers.

hq_gv4.desc: The project has policies for conflicts of interest, vendor participation, and institutional influence.

hq_gv5.desc: The project periodically reviews governance effectiveness and updates policies. The annual review is documented; no completed review is recorded yet.

hq_gv6.desc: The project documents and practices a standard voting procedure for decisions requiring formal approval. No documented voting procedure for decisions that need formal approval.
hq_gv6.note: Gap: no evidence yet. Section: Governance & Decision-Making.

hq_gv7.desc: The project has an adopted, documented process for resolving community or governance disputes. The Code of Conduct covers conduct, but there is no process for resolving technical or governance disputes.
hq_gv7.note: Gap: no evidence yet. Section: Governance & Decision-Making.

hq_ce1.desc: The project identifies its target users, contributors, adopters, and stakeholder communities.

hq_ce2.desc: The project provides welcoming contribution pathways for non-code and code contributors.

hq_ce3.desc: The project has public communication channels with clear participation norms.

hq_ce4.desc: The project has a code of conduct and an incident response process.

hq_ce5.desc: The project measures and responds to community health indicators. Activity is measured (merged PRs, npm downloads, release velocity). Community health indicators such as response times and contributor retention are not, and weekly issue triage is still planned.

hq_do1.desc: The project has clear installation, configuration, and upgrade documentation. Install and setup are documented; upgrade documentation is thin while the docs site is being rebuilt.

hq_do2.desc: The project provides end-user documentation appropriate to its primary audiences. End-user docs exist but are mid-rebuild; the ecosystem doc site and Learn HAX are the planned replacement.

hq_do3.desc: The project documents contributor onboarding, development environment setup, and review workflows.

hq_do4.desc: The project maintains architecture and integration documentation. The ecosystem web itself is the planned living architecture map.

hq_do5.desc: Documentation is maintained as part of the release and contribution process. A weekly docs drift pass is planned but not running yet.

hq_po1.desc: The project publishes a roadmap or planning process that communicates priorities and timelines. The roadmap names directions but not timelines.
hq_po1.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Project Operations & Roadmap.

hq_po2.desc: The project uses a public issue tracker with triage, labels, and response expectations.

hq_po3.desc: The project follows a predictable release process with changelogs and versioning.

hq_po4.desc: The project has defined support channels and support boundaries.

hq_po5.desc: The project tracks maintainership capacity and bus factor risks. Succession is documented; maintainer capacity and bus factor are not tracked over time.
hq_po5.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Project Operations & Roadmap.

hq_sr1.desc: The project has a documented security policy and private vulnerability reporting process.

hq_sr2.desc: The project uses automated testing, dependency scanning, and continuous integration.

hq_sr3.desc: The project manages software supply chain integrity for releases. Confirm signed tags are in place in every core repo.

hq_sr4.desc: The project documents privacy, data handling, and compliance-relevant practices.

hq_sr5.desc: The project has an incident response and post-incident learning process.

hq_as1.desc: The project follows accessibility standards and includes accessibility in testing and release review. Element suites include axe checks; contrast, dark mode and reduced-motion gates are planned as blocking.

hq_as2.desc: The project supports relevant education technology standards and documents interoperability.

hq_as3.desc: The project provides APIs, export options, or data portability mechanisms. Sites are plain files; import and export cover PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, Markdown and EPUB.

hq_as4.desc: The project supports localization, internationalization, or adaptation for diverse institutional contexts when relevant. Interface in more than 100 languages.

hq_as5.desc: The project documents supported platforms, browsers, devices, and deployment environments.

hq_ai1.desc: The project describes its value proposition and use cases for higher education stakeholders.
hq_ai1.note: Evidenced. Section: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit.

hq_ai2.desc: The project provides evidence of adoption, deployments, or community use.
hq_ai2.note: Evidenced. Section: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit.

hq_ai3.desc: The project supports evaluation, pilots, and procurement due diligence. hax.cloud offers a no-install demo, but there are no HECVAT-style procurement answers or a pilot guide.
hq_ai3.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit.

hq_ai4.desc: The project documents implementation services, hosting options, or support partners when available. Hosting options exist (HAXiam, Reclaim Hosting, Docker images) but no single page lists hosting and support partners.
hq_ai4.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit.

hq_ai5.desc: The project collects user feedback and uses it to improve product direction. Feedback arrives through issues and Merlin; a structured user study is planned.
hq_ai5.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Adoption, Impact & Institutional Fit.

hq_fs1.desc: The project identifies current and needed resources for maintenance, governance, support, and growth.

hq_fs2.desc: The project has a funding, membership, sponsorship, or institutional support model.

hq_fs3.desc: The project has a plan for post-grant or post-founder continuity.

hq_fs4.desc: The project maintains transparent infrastructure ownership and operational dependencies.

hq_fs5.desc: The project periodically assesses sustainability risks and publishes improvement priorities. One assessment has been run (haxcms-php). There is no recurring reassessment or published improvement priority list yet.
hq_fs5.note: Partly evidenced. Section: Financial & Organizational Sustainability.

tours.label: HEOSAT, question by question
tours.message: 47 questions in 9 sections: 33 evidenced, 12 partial, 2 gaps.

scenes.caption: Apereo publishes HEOSAT. HAX runs it with AI through the heosat skill in PRAW, a process worked out with Apereo.
Partly evidenced: mostly docs mid-rebuild, procurement answers, and reviews documented but not yet held.

The gaps: GV6, The project documents and practices a standard voting procedure for decisions requiring formal approval; GV7, The project has an adopted, documented process for resolving community or governance disputes.
A win: HAX's HEOSAT work helped fellow project BookLooky go through Apereo incubation more accurately.
